chapter: After Cab: Don Redman, teaching and records
title: Teaching studio with Cozy Cole and his pupils
summary: Thomas and Cozy Cole open a 48th Street studio, he advertises as ex-Cab, and teaches Wyler and Buddy Stafford.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: So I just kept teaching, and I got my little break with Joe Davis to...
You were teaching?
Yeah, I had my studio. See, I started teaching...
This is something I want to know about. What did you do after Cab? You had a studio.
Yes. Cozy and I got a studio together.
Good. Now, where was that studio?
On 48th Street, right across from Manny's.
Who were some of your pupils?
Well, one thing I did, I advertised. I advertised in Metronome and in Downbeat. And I had the sense to capitalize on being with Cab. So I said, 'Walter
Thomas - 150
'Foots' Thomas, formerly with Cab Calloway, teaching saxophone."

And I taught a lot of young guys. I had a couple of guys that got into Jazz. But one guy told me later on that he played by ear. I put a lesson over to him, then that sucker would come in the next lesson and play the lesson. And I thought he was reading! He told me years later that he never learned how to read. He was one of the good Jazz players; I can't think of his name right now. But I taught...
Can you remember any other guys?

Well, I can tell you some of the stars I gave lessons to. The one guy who played.... I can't think of his name now. He played with this singing group, them brothers... They were brothers who had a band, and he was the alto player, and I taught him. I only gave him a few lessons, because he was in town with Les Brown's band. Doris Day's first husband. His name was Wyler. He had studied with Merle, and when he came to New York with the band, he studied...
What about Buddy Stafford?
Well, Buddy Stafford and I studied with Merle together. See, we studied with Merle at the same time. We got to be very friendly. He was a great musician. And
Thomas - 151
there's a guy who didn't really know how good he was. Buddy?
He found out later, but he...
He drank, yeah. But he really didn't know how good he was. I had taught...
He was a very fine player.
yeah, he was great. Played flute... He finally passed on, you know.
Did he?
Yeah, he moved down to Florida, went down there for two or three months. But he was a good friend of mine.
